item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating temporal sensitivity from ranking accuracy. CETRec (2025) distinguishes absolute order—recency—from relative order between interactions, using counterfactual tuning to strengthen both in LLM recommenders ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047)). Genetic-algorithm counterfactual explanations (2025) search for minimal history edits that change recommendations; useful for identifying influential interactions, but their reported fidelity concerns model behavior, not verified user preferences ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606)). RecSys 2026 research finds history-aware pairwise models outperform SASRec/eSASRec reproductions on four of five benchmarks, showing that strong accuracy need not imply higher-order sequence reasoning; those datasets differ from the four categories here ([authors’ report](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling)).\n\nDiagnostic synthesis: compare removal of repeated recent interest evidence against isolated interactions, defining similarity only from available titles/descriptions or training interactions. Include equal-size random removals matched on position and popularity; distinguish masking from deletion because deletion also shifts positions. Test order separately with local swaps, prefix shuffles retaining the latest item, and reversal. Use substitutions matched on popularity and semantic similarity to distinguish interest changes from generic corruption. Measure original-target rank changes, top-10 overlap, and shifts toward the perturbed interest; report paired uncertainty and results by history length/category. These are proposed controls, not an established validated protocol from the cited papers. Excess sensitivity to isolated events suggests brittle reliance; weak response to repeated recent evidence suggests insufficient interest aggregation. Such patterns motivate sequence-encoding or training-objective ablations, but interventions on observed histories establish model dependence—not causal effects on users or latent conformity/diversity traits."}
